applied.problem: "On its own it is a machine that turns" is absolute, but a pressure gauge is also a circle (a smaller one, drawn in this very lesson), so the rule would have Dan misread a gauge as a pump or motor.
"A circle turns" is absolute, yet the gauge the lesson teaches is a circle that does not turn; narrowed so the step stays true on a real sheet.
The tray label "A circle is a machine that turns" contradicts the gauge on the shelf and on Screen 13, a circle that does not turn; narrowed to match the explanation.
In ISO 1219-1 parts built as one unit are enclosed by a chain line of long dashes and dots, not a dashed line; a dashed line is a pilot or drain line, as the lesson itself teaches.
